_comment: Config-as-IP (docs/vertical_engines/VERTICAL_MODULE_PATTERN.md; docs/vertical_engines/11-inventory-engine.md 'Config keys' -- inventory-reorder-points.json): nce/vertical_modules/inventory/replenishment.py's do_recommend_restock (Module 11, Wave 6 -- restock-advisor) reads this for per-SKU reorder-point thresholds -- business logic, not code. GLOBAL, not namespace-scoped, for this wave -- mirrors inventory-valuation.json's own choice (docs/vertical_engines/11-inventory-engine.md's 'per-tenant' language is the older spec; a per-namespace override is not built here, same honest scope limit inventory-valuation.json states for itself). 'reorder_points' lists ONLY the SKUs this tenant has bothered to tune a threshold for -- do_recommend_restock never invents a default for a SKU absent from this map; an absent SKU is reported with reorder_point=null and recommended=false rather than a guessed policy (see the module's own docstring 'Config is IP' section for the full fallback rationale). Values are plain JSON numbers, quantised to inventory_transactions.delta's own 3dp scale on load -- same discipline as inventory-valuation.json/do_valuation's Decimal coercion. 'consumption_lookback_days' bounds the ledger window do_recommend_restock reads for its consumption-velocity figure -- carried here (rather than as an NCE_INVENTORY_REORDER_LOOKBACK_DAYS env key per docs/engines/inventory-admin.md 4.1's planned default of 30) because nce/config.py is explicitly out of scope for this wave (see this wave's own orchestrator amendments); the default below matches that same planned value so the two do not silently diverge if/when Batch 134b or a later wave adds the env key. Only an ABSENT 'consumption_lookback_days' falls back to 30: a value that is PRESENT but non-positive is rejected with a ValueError, never coalesced away. 0 and 30 are different instructions -- silently answering 0 with a 30-day window (and reporting consumption_lookback_days: 30 back to the caller) would contradict this file; a negative value is worse still, putting the lookback cutoff in the FUTURE so consumption_velocity_qty is pinned at 0.000 and ledger_rows at [] with no error and a rationale that reads exactly as if nothing had been consumed.
